name: Research Ethics Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building research ethics — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary research ethics tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building research ethics — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary research ethics tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When research ethics guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Validate research ethics outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. Check that research ethics terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. When multiple research ethics strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
5. Keep research ethics changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to research ethics (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Before starting research ethics work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
8. Measure before optimizing any research ethics bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
9. Document any non-obvious research ethics decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
10. Keep research ethics outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
11. State assumptions about research ethics explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new research ethics abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop research ethics edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting research ethics assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these research ethics guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
